title: Leave empty statement caches virtual
impact: Exp 267 raised the per-connection statement cache to 128 entries and measured +0.8-1.2 MB peak RSS, attributing it to the larger fixed entry arrays. The actual 2,136-byte entry makes one cache 273,408 bytes, and optimized arm64 code revealed the more immediate cause: although `resqlite_db` is allocated with `calloc`, `stmt_cache_init` zeroed the entire array again. The compiler removed the adjacent writer clear but retained one 273,408-byte `bzero` in the reader-open loop, so a normal four-reader open eagerly touched 1,093,632 bytes before any statement used a slot. Initializing only `count = 0` is safe because lookup and cleanup inspect only entries below count and every insertion fully zeroes its slot before publishing it. Across twelve alternating-order fresh-process passes, max RSS fell 589,824 bytes at two readers and 1,056,768 bytes at four; open-growth RSS fell 540,672 and 974,848 bytes, with the candidate lower in all 48 paired observations and reader-count scaling broadly consistent with the assembly prediction. Six alternating-order AOT wall passes improved native open by 2.4% at two readers and 2.7% at four, with no candidate-slower pass above 1.6%. Full-cache and eviction controls (`point1`, `rotate128`, `churn-unique`) stayed within 0.7% in aggregate, and 23 focused tests covering empty/first-slot use, 400-statement eviction, dependency reliability and native allocation faults passed. This recovers most of exp 267's memory price with one deleted clear and no new allocation, OOM or ownership path; exact-sized dependency metadata is now justified only by a representative populated-cache footprint, not empty-open RSS.
